To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
InP-based QD can be used in biology, but their application should be preceded by a detailed study of the interaction with cells and the mechanisms of QD internalization.
the fluorescence quantum yield and stability of InP-based QD are lower than those of CdSe QDs.
InP/Zn-S QDs with PEG-COOH shell are less photostable than CdSe/Zn-S QD with PEG-COONH2 shell.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the study of the effect of the chemical modifications of the organic shells of QDs on the interaction of these particles with cells of different origins, and it is the first study of InP-based QD interaction with biological objects.
the development of new methods and approaches to the synthesis, functionalization and application of semiconductor QDs.
the study of the photophysical and cytotoxic properties of InP-based QD.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the QDs-COOP are the most promising for biological applications.
QDs with a core of InP and a shell of ZnS are promising for use in biology and medicine.
the InP-based QD-PEG-COOHS are the most promising for biological research, because of the lowest cytotoxicity and good spectral-luminescence characteristics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the QDs-PEG-NH2 have the highest toxicity, QDs-PEG without reactive groups are slightly less toxic, while QDs-PEG with carboxylic group are practically not toxic.
the use of InP-based QD is promising for further biological applications, but it requires further optimization of the shell structure.
the use of InP-based QD is a promising alternative to cadmium-based QDs, but the further optimization of the synthesis and surface functionalization of InP-based particles is necessary.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the chemical modifications of the surface organic shell of QDs have a significant impact on their biological properties.
the choice of the organic shell is an important factor affecting the interaction with cells of various origins and the efficiency of QD use.
the choice of a QDs coating with specific functional groups is of crucial importance in order to achieve the desired biological effect.
